blocks.content: depends_on controls the order services start in, but it is frequently misunderstood, by default it only waits for a container to start, not for the application inside it to actually be ready.
Listing depends_on: [db] on an app service tells Compose to start the db container before starting app, a straightforward way to make sure dependencies come up first.

blocks.alt: A dependency starts first, before the service that needs it

blocks.content:
services:
  app:
    depends_on: [db]
  db:
    image: postgres:15

code.content:
services:
  app:
    depends_on: [db]
  db:
    image: postgres:15

codes.yaml:
services:
  app:
    depends_on: [db]
  db:
    image: postgres:15

blocks.content: 2. The Common Gotcha: Started Is Not the Same as Ready
blocks.text: 2. The Common Gotcha: Started Is Not the Same as Ready

blocks.content: By default, depends_on only waits for the db container process to start, not for Postgres inside it to actually finish initializing and start accepting connections. An app service that assumes the database is ready the instant it starts can fail with connection errors on a cold start, a genuinely common source of confusing, intermittent startup failures.

blocks.alt: A started container is not necessarily a ready one

blocks.content: The real fix combines depends_on with a condition, specifically service_healthy, which waits for that dependency's healthcheck (covered in the next topic) to actually pass, not just for the process to have started.

blocks.alt: Waiting for a real, passing health check, not just a started process

blocks.content:
services:
  app:
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "pg_isready"]

code.content:
services:
  app:
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "pg_isready"]

codes.yaml:
services:
  app:
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "pg_isready"]

blocks.content: If depends_on is omitted entirely, Compose makes no guarantee about start order at all, services may start in any order, or concurrently, which can surface the exact same "dependency not ready yet" problem, just less predictably.

blocks.alt: No declared order means no guarantee at all

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: depends_on controls container start order, but by default only waits for the dependency to start, not for the application inside it to be ready.
Combining depends_on with condition: service_healthy is what actually waits for a dependency to be genuinely ready, via its healthcheck.
